title: Accidents, Near Misses & RIDDOR
whatItIs: RIDDOR 2013 is the law that requires certain work-related accidents, diseases and dangerous occurrences (near misses) to be reported and recorded.

keyFacts.text: Deaths and specified injuries MUST be notified without delay; report within 10 days.
Over-7-day injuries to workers MUST be reported within 15 days of the accident.
Over-3-day injuries MUST be recorded, but needn't be reported.
A member of the public taken from the scene to hospital for treatment MUST be reported.

keyFacts: The 7 days don't count the accident day, but do count weekends and rest days.

visual.caption: What RIDDOR says must be reported, and when

a.label: Specified injury
points: Eg a fracture (not finger, thumb or toe)

b.label: Over-7-day injury
points: Off normal work over 7 days in a row

onTheTest.question: A worker breaks his arm in a fall from a trestle. When must this be reported under RIDDOR?
options: Only if he's off work over 7 days
Only if kept in hospital overnight
onTheTest.why: A fracture other than to a finger, thumb or toe is a specified injury: notify without delay, with a report received within 10 days.

onTheTest.question: A labourer hurts her back and can't do her normal job for 5 days. What does RIDDOR require?
options: Record it, but it doesn't need reporting
onTheTest.why: Over-3-day injuries must be recorded (the accident book is enough). They're reported only if the incapacity goes on past 7 days.

traps: A precautionary hospital trip with no injury apparent isn't reportable.
A broken finger, thumb or toe isn't a specified injury, but may be an over-7-day injury.
Near misses count: some dangerous occurrences must be reported even if no one is hurt.
